Commentary.Commentary: So that's it from us! We come to the end of an emphatic and dominating series win over the second best Test side in the world. This will surely make a statement, providing plenty of positives and contrastingly, a lot to work on for the touring side. Life was never going to be easy for them post AB de Villiers, and they're now realizing just how difficult that's going to be. Back to the drawing board for the Saffers. Anyhow, we bid you farewell. Hope you enjoyed our coverage. We hope you will join us for future matches. Adios!

Suranga Lakmal, the Sri Lankan skipper, says that they worked hard for this and all this is the result of that. On the way their spinners bowled in this series, he says that they have the best spinners in the world and that's the reason for it. On his captaincy, he states that it was a team effort and he didn't have to do much.

Faf du Plessis, the South African skipper, says that he is happy with how the guys played. He praises de Bruyn and says that it was possible to score runs in the game. Credits the Sri Lankan team for the way they played their cricket. Adds that they have taken a lot of positives from the series like Maharaj's 9-fer and de Bruyn's knock. On the second spinner, he reckons that he should have played another spinner after seeing the way the ball was turning. Suggests that it is helpful in these sub-continent pitches to put on a fight. Ends by saying that he learns from things like this.

Man of the Match and Series, Dimuth Karunaratne, on his batting says that it was easier to bat at the start as the ball came nicely onto the bat but once the pitch became dry, the ball spun a lot. On playing spin, he says that he stuck to the basics by rotating strike and waiting for the loose balls. Ends by saying that they take one series at a time and will look forward to their next against England.

Rangana Herath, who is up for an interview, says that he is very pleased winning the game and the series against the number 2 Test side. Suggests that he is happy to play on any ground and not only SSC and Galle. Reckons that it is easier to bowl with the hard ball as it gives you assistance and the spinners bowled very well during the entire series. About his retirement, he says that he knows about it but will look play the next Test series against India.

De Bruyn and Bavuma put up a gritty century stand, providing a sturdy resistance and even, to some extent, reviving the Proteas' hopes of possibly getting something out of this. But Rangana Herath came to the fore again, like he has so many times and broke that stand, which basically opened the floodgates. The others chipped in and wrapped things up. The veteran finished with 6 wickets. A resounding victory for the hosts. A special mention for de Bruyn though, he was the best batsman in the ranks. Was grinding it out there, looked assured, showed the others how it's done as he went on to score his maiden Test ton.

Now, with already a healthy lead, the Suranga Lakmal-led men piled on the pressure with the openers once again getting the job done, and then Angelo Mathews and Roshen Silva contributed well, with the former scoring a much-needed fifty. A daunting target of 490 was set, one which could be considered as a winning one. The Islanders once again wreaked havoc, with the spinners showing their magic yet again. Almost everyone was knocked over, till Theunis de Bruyn and Temba Bavuma joined forces.

Sri Lanka followed up their good show with the bat when they came out with the ball. The spin trio dismantled the South African batting order and cleaned them right up in no time. Faf du Plessis and Quinton de Kock were the only ones to put up any kind of a fight, but alas cricket is a 11-man sport for a reason. Need everyone to do their part.

Another dominating performance from the hosts has seen them cleansweep South Africa 2-0. It was all Sri Lanka the moment this match started. Actually, you could argue, the match swung in the home side's favour when the Proteas decided to go with just one spinner. Suranga Lakmal won the toss and his team dominated from that point itself. The openers set the tone, then the middle order and even the tail followed suit. Keshav Maharaj sent a spinning wave that crashed them down with 9 wickets, but despite that, the hosts put up a massive first innings total.

OUT! And that seals it! The job is done and SRI LANKA WIN THIS GAME BY 199 RUNS! Steyn jumps out of the crease and looks to go big again. Gets a big, big top edge which skies high in the sky, towards long on. Gunathilaka settles himself under it and ensures Herath finishes with a 6-fer. Handshakes all around, smiles and fist pumps everywhere. A good performance from the Lankans.
Muted appeal, but there's bat involved. Full and straight, the ball raps Steyn on the front pad but not before taking the inside edge. Steyn survives to fight another day.
Fuller and on the stumps, blocked with the full face of the bat.
Quite slow through the air, around off, turns away as Steyn lets it go.

SIX! The tailenders are going to enjoy themselves. Might as well. Tossed up around off, Steyn jumps out of his crease and lofts it high in the air. Gets enough on it to clear the long off boundary for a maximum.
FOUR! That's a shot a top order batsman would be proud of. Picks up the length early and lofts this over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Gets behind the ball and blocks it onto the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Oh! Almost another one. Lands this around off, Lungi looks to defend this nut almost gets the outside edge to the keeper.
Lungi Ngidi is the last man in.

OUT! Nine down! Sri Lanka need just one more wicket to win the match! Dilruwan gives this air and lands it around off, Rabada goes forward and looks to block it. The ball turns and takes the outside edge of the bat. It goes straight to Mathews at first slip who does not drop those.
Fuller in length around off, Rabada prods forward and blocks it down.
Full and slow on the stumps, kept out off the front foot.
Dale Steyn is the next man in to bat.

OUT! Russel Arnold, you beauty! He did mention on the previous ball that the one turning will not get you. The ones which do not turn are those that the batsmen need to be careful about. And Theunis de Bruyn is consumed by that disease which most non-Asian batsmen have. Confusion whether the ball will turn or not, whether it should be played or not. Herath comes from around the wicket and drifts it in from off. Now, because of what happened on the previous ball, de Bruyn thinks it will turn away but it just keeps coming in with the angle. He leaves it and as a result, gets his bails knocked off. Bit of an anti-climatic way to be dismissed as well. South Africa will be disappointed that he got out in such fashion after the knock he's played so far, but he deserves this standing ovation from the crowd and his dressing room. A knock to remember for the all-rounder.
Fuller and spinning away outside off, beaten past the edge. Hmmm... a sly Russel Arnold remarks on air - 'The one which turns will never get you...'
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Straighter one from the bowler, blocked out.

FOUR! Maiden Test century for Theunis de Bruyn! Thoroughly deserved. He's the only player who's looked assured and played a flawless knock so far. It's been tough work, but he's toughened it out so far and done a wonderful job. Full on the stumps, de Bruyn kneels down and paddle sweeps it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Close! Perera drifts it around off, it comes in a bit as Rabada lets it be. Goes really close past the off stick.
Stays behind the line and blocks it out.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Crouches a bit and half-pulls, half-sweeps this fine down the leg side. A bit of a fumble from the fielder allows the batsmen to take two.
Oooh! Beaten this time! Fuller and going across, de Bruyn is forward to defend but the ball doesn't turn and goes past the outside edge.
Edged and away! Dilruwan floats it across around off, de Bruyn plays at it and gets an edge which flies behind. Two good runs taken.
Kagiso has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Probably an inside edge on that. Herath bowls it a bit quicker through the air, on the stumps, Rabada maybe gets an inside edge on this on his pads as it falls just beside short leg.
Not much turn on this, outside off, blocked on the off side.

SIX! First maximum of the innings and it's come off the bat of Kagiso Rabada. Full and right in the slot, Rabada has no qualms about putting this away. Smokes this high over long on and clears the fence with ease.
Full and straight, in line of the stumps, Rabada blocks.
Gives this a lot of flight outside off, Theunis taps it to covers and gets to the other end.
Flicked neatly through mid-wicket. Right in the gap, comfortably two runs result. Good work from Rabada to survive this over.
Another one. Teasing Rabada with the flight and landing it full outside off. He goes for the big drive, gets beaten as Dickwella can't collect cleanly.
A lot of air on this occasion, Rabada drives away from his body and gets beaten past the edge.
Drifting in from around off, Kagiso is solid in defense.
Fuller, slower and outside the line of off stump, Rabada comes forward and shoulders arms.
The helmet and shin guards out. Another fielder coming around the batsman now. So two slips, a short leg and a silly point in place.
Backs away to this shorter ball around off, de Bruyn backs away ans slaps it to covers for a single. Rabada to face almost the entire over now it seems.
FOUR! Superb timing. Almost a yorker darted on off, Rabada with fast hands drills this through mid off and finds the fence.
Quite slow through the air, just outside off, doesn't spin at all and that beats Rabada who plays for the turn.
Full and straight, attacking the stumps, kept out safely.
Swept away through backward square leg for one run.
Landed on a driving length outside off, it's played off the outer half to point.
Tosses it right up there, on the stumps, met with a defensive bat in response.
Rangana Herath has a change of ends. He will take the new ball first up.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and turning away outside off, Rabada goes for the expansive drive but gets beaten.
Slower through the air, around off, kept out off the front foot.
Down leg, nudged towards fine leg. Easy single collected.

Tad risky, that. Landing short and spinning in from around off, de Bruyn backs away to cut but is a bit cramped for room. Manages to get it away through covers, but still a little risky. Two to the total.
From around the wicket, it's full on middle and off, de Bruyn is forward in defense.
Dilruwan Perera on now.
FOUR! Full toss around off, Rabada stands tall and smashes it straight back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Loopy and full in length, blocked.
Stays right behind the line and blocks it out.
A bit short on off, spins away sharply. Rabada goes back and defends it right under his nose.
Quite full on leg, hits Rabada on the pads. Light appeal, but it was always going down leg.
From around the wicket, it's floated on middle and off. Drifts in, then turns and beats the outside edge of Rabada's bat.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Shortish around off, cut this towards the backward point fielder for an easy single.
Fuller ball on middle, played back to the bowler.
Edge but falls short of the fielder at first slip. Rabada waits for the ball to come at him then throws his bat ahead in defense. He gets an edge to the first slip region. No harm done.
Play and miss from Rabada. Serves this around off, Rabada hangs back and doesn't get behind the ball.
Stays in his crease and defends the ball off his back foot.
Pushes this ball towards mid on and takes a quick run.
No feet movement and Rabada pokes at it. Once again cannot put bat to ball.
This one keeps low. KG stays inside and looks to block it outside off but the ball goes under his bat.
Turn again. Pitches this on middle and off, it spins away from Kagiso who plays and misses.
Turn and bounce. Rabada goes forward to block it but cannot make contact.
Works this away with a wristy shot to the on side for a run.
Akila Dananjaya will bowl from the other end.
Tossed up on middle, well blocked by Rabada.

We are back after our light lunch! The hosts just need 3 more wickets to win this game and the series. For the visitors, it is just about how long they can prolong this. De Bruyn is strangled on 85 and would like to get to that three digit figure. Meanwhile, Herath will finish his over and Kagiso Rabada is the new man in.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Though, credit to Bavuma and de Bruyn till now. They made the Lankans toil hard for the wickets. It went to the point that we saw Suranga Lakmal bowling for the first time in the game. The pair showed a lot of stomach to fight and kept digging it in there. De Bruyn is still fighting, but not sure how long will his resistance last now. Join us at 1240 local (0710 GMT) for what could be the final session of this game.

Heartbreak for South Africa. All the hard work done by Temba Bavuma and Theunis de Bruyn could come crashing down in no time now. The pair added 123 runs between them, completing their respective fifties in the process, and almost saw the session through. But... but... Rangana Herath decided to show his magic and undid all the good work by the pair. It all changed in the final three overs of the session, when the veteran left-armer dismissed Bavuma and then de Kock in his following over. Sri Lanka are in the tail and it might just be a matter of when now.

OUT! It's umpire's call! Quinton de Kock is out of here! Rangana Herath strikes yet again. Served outside off, spinning in and de Kock goes back to defend. A big mistake, he should have come forward, as he gets beaten for pace and caught on the pads. Loud appeal goes up and the finger is raised. The left-hander decides to review it, as he should, and it's taken upstairs. Replays show the impact is umpire's call as the ball is clipping leg and the decision stands. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Big moment in the game. Quinton de Kock is caught leg before and he immediately reviews. This could decide the game right here...
Spins down leg, beats de Kock who tries to reverse sweep again. Off the pads and to leg slip.
Flat, quick and short on off, whipped off the back foot through to mid on for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and just outside off, met with a straight bat in defense.
Comes half-forward to this one and defends it out.
Outside off, shorter in length, kept out off the back foot.
Drifting in at first before turning away, beats the outside edge of de Kock's hanging bat. The southpaw is lucky he didn't nick it behind.
Short and flat outside off, punched crisply through the gap in the covers. A couple results.
That's turned square! Wowza. Tossed up on middle, it turns so much that it goes past the edge of de Kock's bat and rises straight to first slip.
Maybe going down a touch too much. Slider coming in with the arm, raps de Kock on the pads who goes back to work it on the leg side. Muted appeal, but it's turned down.
Full around off, met with a defensive blade in response.
Attempts the reverse sweep again, a bit dangerously this time, as Herath drags the length back a touch. Off the pads, past leg slip and a leg bye is taken.
Floated on off, blocked by getting his front leg out of the way.
Full and flighted outside off, another reverse sweep from Quinton de Kock, through point this time. He'll get a couple of runs for it.
FOUR! Loopy from over the wicket and full on off, de Kock gets low and reverse sweeps it through backward point for a boundary. Seems he's come right out of the nets.
Quinton de Kock is the new man in.

OUT! Rangana Herath, as he so often does, comes up with the breakthrough when his team really needs it. A peach of a delivery to dismiss Temba Bavuma. Beauty! Comes from around the wicket and tosses it up on middle and off, it turns, just the right amount and takes the edge of Bavuma's bat, who's forward to defend. Dickwella does well to take a low catch and break this 123-run stand. A good knock from Bavuma, he did well to hang in there, but his stay is over now. The beginning of the end for South Africa too?
Shortish on the pads again, nicely flicked through square leg for another run. Five singles of this over and all of them easily taken and worked.
On the pads, flicked through the on side. One run taken.
Out comes the conventional sweep. This time it's Bavuma. He works it to deep square leg for a run.
Whippy reverse sweep from de Bruyn. How effective this shot has been for them? A flatter ball on middle worked through backward point for a run.
Shortish around off, Temba waits for the turn and then works it to square leg for a run.
Around the wicket, floated on off and Bavuma charges forward to defend it.
Theunis has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Similar delivery from Herath and easily kept out again by de Bruyn.
Tossed up, slower on a length, blocked off the front foot.
Flighted around off, worked to the off side.
On off, easily defended.
Flatter on middle, flicked to the on side for a run.
Change of ends for Rangana Herath.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Good batting from Bavuma. He uses his feet to get close to the pitch and drives it down the ground through mid off for a boundary.
Worked to mid-wicket. No run taken.

Oooh! Close. Full and going across outside off, Bavuma goes low to drag the sweep but the ball ricochets off the bottom edge onto his boot then onto the track. The ball lobs behind and it lands just short of first slip.

FOUR BYES! The pitch is misbehaving a bit from time to time. Down leg, shooting off the surface and spinning, the keeper can't catch it as the batsman went for the sweep but missed it. Goes right behind for a boundary.
From around the wicket, it's fuller on the pads, it's swept just wide of backward square leg by Bavuma for a double.
Dilruwan Perera has a change of ends.
Bit fullish in length on middle and leg, defended down in front of short leg.
Worked to short leg from the back foot.
Pitches around leg, spins down as the batsman leaves it alone. Dickwella can't collect properly as it goes behind off his gloves. The batsmen take two byes.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Continues from around the wicket, lands it on a shorter length, catches Bavuma on the pads as he misses his flick.
A bit shortish on middle and leg, worked to mid-wicket.
Danushka Gunathilaka is on to bowl now.
Waits for the ball to come before going back and cutting it down towards third man with the spin. A brace taken.
Fuller on off with some turn, de Bruyn gets a leading edge, safely, towards mid off.
Just behind a driving length, outside off, makes Theunis reach forward a bit to keep it out.
Spinning away outside off, covers the line and lets it be.
Drifting in at first, around off, spins away as de Bruyn pushes it to covers.
Tossed up from around the wicket, on middle and leg, swept neatly through to deep backward square leg for a run.
Safely ends the over with a front foot block. Didn't allow the ball to turn at all.
Right behind the line of this one. Fuller on off, defended well.
Hit on the arm, outside the line of off stump. Perera serves it around off, it spins and kicks off.
Rocks back in a flash and slaps the punch through to sweeper cover. A comfortable two results.
Full and loopy, around off, blocked tightly.
Flatter and shorter on middle and off, de Bruyn moves across, gets behind the line and defends it right under his nose.
Bavuma is rock solid in defense as he comes half forward and brings his bat ahead of his pad to block.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Works it away with the wrists on the leg side. No run taken.
Spinning away from outside off, left alone.
Short, it's pulled hard and connected well too. Temba is unfortunate to have found the square leg fielder.
Tossed up delivery on off, blocked off the front foot on the off side.
Sharp turn for Dilruwan. Lands it on off, spins in from a bit of a shorter length and de Bruyn doesn't pick it up. He goes back to cut, but gets hit high on the thigh pad.
Goes deep inside the crease, waits for the ball to turn before keeping it down in front of short leg.

The 100-run stand is up! Vital for the Proteas. Good fight shown from these two. One wonders, had one or two more provided a similar display, things might have turned out different. Bavuma sweeps this through backward square leg for one.
Darted full on middle stump, de Bruyn gets low to reverse sweep but gets a bottom edge which bumps on the track and bounces over the slip fielder's head. Single taken.
Touch short on off, turning in, kept out on the leg side.
Looped up by the offie, de Bruyn blocks by getting well forward.
Dilruwan Perera is back on.
Played to point intentionally this time. Dot ball.
Closes the face a bit too early there. Fuller and outside off, Bavuma gets a leading edge square on the off side. No harm done.
Bavuma tries to get down the track but Rangi drags his length back. So the batsman goes back and plays it towards point.
Full and slow from the bowler, guarded out without any trouble.
Turning away slightly, gently tossed up, Temba with a tame push to covers.
Thrown well outside off, no shot offered by the batsman.
Full and straight, easily kept out.
The leg break this time but de Bruyn picks it up early. Prods forward and blocks it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Plays this out off the back foot for nothing.

FOUR! Wonderful execution from Theunis de Bruyn to get this away. Brings out the reverse sweep to this fuller ball and places it through cover-point. Roshen Silva at sweeper cover moves a long way to his left, dives to stop it but he can't. Boundary.
Spinning in on leg, Bavuma flicks it through the vacant leg slip position. In the air, but safe. Single collected.
Driven to cover. End of the over.
Darts it full and fast, jammed out by the batsman.
A lot of flight on this, Theunis is forward to block.

Almost unplayable! What a jaffa! Jeez. De Bruyn survives a scare. Herath drops it a bit short and this ball spins and kicks off the deck like it's nobody's business. Theunis initially goes to play, but does well to go back and sway away from the line.
Loopy and fuller, outside off, pushed into the covers.
Fifty for Temba Bavuma! His 11th in this format. Well-deserved too. Done well under pressure. Sweeps this to square leg and takes a single to get to the milestone.
Rangana Herath comes back on.
Too full again, easy enough for de Bruyn to come forward and negotiate the spin.
Tossed up off break turning in, Theunis is forward in defense.
Stays right back and keeps it out.
Full and just outside off, Bavuma drags the sweep through square leg and rotates strike.
Would have been better had he come forward, but he goes back instead and blocks it out as there's no turn.
Heavy turn for Akila. Turning in, de Bruyn works it through the gap in the mid-wicket region and takes one.
Too full and outside off, Bavuma gets low for the reverse sweep and gets hit low on the pads. Impact is outside off.
Turned off the pads, wide of short leg. One more run to the total.
All too comfortable for this Protea pair now. Bavuma whips this off the back foot to deep mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Spinning down the leg side on a shorter length, de Bruyn moves inside the crease and places it through backward square leg for one.
Gives this some more air on the stumps, blocked back down the track.
Tossed up delivery on leg stump, Bavuma flicks it off his pads and works it through square leg. A single results and the 200 comes up for South Africa.

He has used his height and reach to great effect through his innings. Again he comes way forward to the fuller ball around off and creams the drive through covers for a couple of runs. This pair looks in total control at the moment.
Too full, pushed to the on side.
Prods forward and keeps it out off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter outside off, reverse swept through cover-point by de Bruyn. A brace results.

Uuf! How would you play such deliveries? Bavuma has played it the best way he could. A flighted ball on length, it hits some rough or bounces from the seam and it just takes off. It almost reaches the grille of the batsman who does well to get his glove in the way and push it to the off side aerially. End result, one run taken from cover-point.

Drinks!  Excellent session for South Africa. They have scored 55 runs in this little session without losing a wicket, probably the first time in this series. The older ball seems easier to play as compared to the new cherry. Let's see for how long these two can continue to bat. It will surely send some jitters in the Lankan camp.
Defended off the front foot by Theunis presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide! Rough patches on the track coming into play. It lands outside leg and takes off from there. Dickwella behinds the sticks does well to collect that.
Wrists the slower ball to the on side for nothing.
On the off stumps, driven to covers by de Bruyn.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle, blocked.
Quick and flat, some spin but going down the leg side. Left alone.
Dhananjaya de Silva is on.
Too full, driven to mid on for no run.

Easily negotiated by Theunis. He has made the bowler bowl to him in an area where he could score runs. Akila isn't getting his rhythm right perhaps. He lands this a bit shortish on middle and it spins further away to the leg side. Theunis flicks it to square leg and takes a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gets behind the line of this one and blocks it.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
Clever stuff from Bavuma! A shortish ball around off, Bavuma punches it off the back foot to mid on and seeing Perera slow to react there, he calls his partner for a quick single. Excellent stuff!
On a back of a length around off, easily blocked by Theunis.
Straightish in line of the stumps, shortish and flicked to fine leg for a run.
On a length just outside off, punched to covers.
Outside off on a length, left alone.
Around off, on a back of a length, blocked.
Bavuma misses the wild hoick across the line. A pull to a not-so-short delivery outside off.
In line of the stumps, kept out easily.
Swept with intent to the square leg region for another single.
On middle and leg, flicked from the inner half of the bat to the on side. One run taken.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Another tossed up off spinner from Akila. Theunis prods forward to play it but fails to get his bat behind the line. The ball hits his pad and goes to forward short leg. The bowler asks a question but the umpire rightly denies.
Flighted on length, defended off the back foot.
Fraction straight in line, de Bruyn moves inside the line and works it to mid-wicket to keep strike.
Just behind a length, quite close to off, kept out safely.
FOUR! Some pace on offer and the batsman takes full advantage of it. Short of a length on off, de Bruyn camps on the back foot and muscles the pull over mid-wicket for a boundary.

Overthrows! A bit sloppy from the Lankans. De Bruyn pushes this just wide of mid on and takes off. Karunaratne rushes to the ball, fires a direct hit at the bowler's end but Theunis is well in. The ball ricochets off the stumps and there's nobody backing up there. So the batsmen take an extra run.
Served on a length again, on the stumps, blocked back down the track.
Back of a length delivery outside off, de Bruyn stands tall and punches it in front of cover.
Hello! Hello! Look at what we have here. Suranga Lakmal is going to be bowling for the first time in this Test. Probably goes to show how good this Protea pair, particularly de Bruyn, has been.
Floats this one Akila, Theunis mistimes his cut and gets it to point. A run taken.
Outside leg, left alone.
Rocks back to the shortish delivery on middle and hits it back to the bowler.
Uses his hands and works this one wide of short leg.
Blocks it back to the bowler.
Theunis looks to sweep the ball from outside off but gets hit on his pad. It hits him outside off so no problems.

FOUR! Out comes the sweep once again. It has been so effective for the visitors throughout. Bavuma sweeps the full ball and connects it really well. A boundary results through the backward square leg region.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shortish in length from Herath, Bavuma moves back to flick it but gets hit on his pad outside leg.
Pitched outside leg, Temba pads it to the off side. Herath bowled this from over the wicket.
No trouble in handling the straighter ball. Easily defended.
Shows the full face of the bat and blocks it nicely.

Prodigious spin. Was there an edge on this? The umpire doesn't think so. It is shortish on middle and leg, Theunis moves back to work it to the leg side but misses it. The spin from around the wicket for Dananjaya takes it away. Two byes result from the fine leg region.
Comes forward to play this one but the spin enables the ball to hit him on his pad.

FOUR! It had Rahul Dravid written on this shot. Cracker! Akila again bowls it short around off, de Bruyn rocks back and punches it handsomely from there. The ball races through wide mid off for the second boundary of the over.
On the pads, flicked to fine leg. One run taken.
Hangs back to defend the shortish delivery on the on side. He looks assured now.
FOUR! Not the kind of delivery you should bowl first. A shortish ball outside off, a lot of width and Temba Bavuma rocks back to cut it. The ball goes through cover-point and a boundary results.
Akila Dananjaya is brought into the attack for the first time today.
Gets behind this one nicely and blocks it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Ooh! All these balls missing the outside edges remind me of Maharaj. He didn't have much luck in the third innings. Herath is going through the same phase. A ripper on off getting Theunis forward and going away from the face of the bat - but beating the outside edge.
In line of the stumps, kept out.
Tossed up outside off, Temba goes with hard hands and gets an outside edge but it goes past the slip fielder. One run taken from the third man region.
He has done this consistently. Another angled in ball on off, it lands and turns away sharply to beat Bavuma on the outside.
On middle and leg, swept to fine leg for another run. These two look sure while batting now.

Punched to covers off the back foot by Bavuma. He takes a double and brings up the fifty-run stand between the duo. Second of the innings for South Africa and perhaps more authoritative than the first one.
Shortish on the pads, flicked through the on side. It looks easy to bat right now.
De Bruyn works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Floated around off, it spins in and raps Theunis on the pad and lobs in the air. The catch is taken at short leg but there was no bat on it.
Shortish on off, tucked to mid-wicket. One run results.
Easily negotiated by Theunis off the front foot to end the over.
Uppish but safe. On the pads from Herath, Bavuma flicks it and gets it in the fine leg region. One run taken.
Around off, Bavuma gets it to the off side off the front foot.
Fuller this time, flick shot missed by the batsman. Gets rapped on the pads as a result.
Flights this one on leg, Temba keeps it out easily.
Slower in line of the stumps, defended.
Worked off the pads again, no run taken.
Landing on middle and leg, turning with some extra bounce, Theunis moves inside the line and blocks it out.
Straightening up a shade after landing, on the stumps, de Bruyn stays back and blocks it out.
Works it off his pads and plays it on the leg side.

FOUR! Maiden Test fifty for Theunis de Bruyn! Brings it up in good style. A well-deserved one too, he's fought hard out there. Angling across outside off, de Bruyn backs away and punches it crisply through the covers for a boundary. Needless to say, he would want to carry on long.
Short and flat outside off, turning in, Bavuma goes back and offers a punch to the cover area. One run taken.
Soft hands helped him there. Spinning delivery away from de Bruyn, he pokes at it and gets an outside edge past slip.
Gets forward and low and keeps it out to the on side.
Outside off, left alone.
Too much spin again. De Bruyn stays away from this one. Herath bowls this in with the angle and it spins away to the hands of the keeper.
Can't do much about it. De Bruyn did well to get behind the line but it spins away from the face of the bat. A rippa!
Out comes the sweep again. It has been effective. Herath pushes it in flatter and lands it on middle. The ball goes to the man at deep square leg for a run.

FOUR OVERTHROWS! Bonus for Bavuma and South Africa. Full and around off, Temba pushes it wide of mid on and sets off for a quick single. Danushka Gunathilaka comes charging in from mid on, gets to the ball, picks it up and has a shy at the stumps at the bowler's end - all in one motion, which is very good. But the throw is way off track and there is no one backing up either. All the way she goes to the cover fence.

NOT OUT. 'The good thing with the review is that... if it is not caught, then you can check for LBW as well,' chuckles Roshan Abeysinghe on air. However, neither is out and the Lankans lose their review. Full and outside off, Bavuma lunges a long way down the track and looks to defend but misses. The ball spins in, goes off his pads and lobs straight to short leg. The Lankans are confident as always though I am not sure the appeal is for what... okay... caught, they say. Lakmal wants it reviewed and well, no edge at all and on checking the LBW, impact was umpire's call but the ball was hitting the 10th stump which usually does not exist in cricket...
Referral for a catch out taken. Temba Bavuma the man  in question for a bat-pad. Is he gone?
On middle and leg, helped down the leg side for one.
A little bit of luck. Bavuma stretches out to sweep this one, gets some top edge but it falls safely around square leg. A run taken.
A tad short, Theunis initially comes forward but then goes back and works it between leg slip and short leg for a single.
Full and outside off, de Bruyn lunges and defends.
And another miss. Similar delivery from Herath, Temba looks to play the line but gets beaten again.
Spins away from the outside edge of Bavuma's bat. No harm done.
Defends it back to Herath.
Straighter one. Bavuma misses the line and gets beaten on the inside.
Defended to the off side off the front foot.
Gets back and keeps it away from his body.
Another off break going down leg. It hits him on his pads and lobs towards leg slip for nothing.
High! Some bounce on this one, it struck Theunis high on the pad.
Looks to sweep and works it to the leg side for no run.
The ball has struck Theunis hard on his hand. Some extra bounce on offer for the bowler.
Too much spin again. It lands on a fullish length, spins in and de Bruyn gets an inside edge onto his pads while defending. No harm done.
Comes forward to play the tossed up ball and works it through mid-wicket. A run taken.
Lunges forward to the last ball and keeps it out easily.
In line of the stumps, pushed to the on side off the back foot.
Around off, blocked.
Temba paddles the ball down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Bavuma defends it from within the crease.
Very effective. The South Africans have come out with some intent this morning. A fuller ball on middle and leg, Bavuma sweeps it with a punch and gets it fine. A brace results.
Rangana Herath to bowl from the other end.
Lunges forward to play the flatter delivery back to the bowler. End of the first over of the session.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Too much spin from the good length area, it goes further away from the right-hander down the leg side.
In line of the stumps, defended.
Around middle, swept to fine leg for a run.
Shortish around off, Bavuma gets a thick edge past slip. The day starts in a similar fashion.
The players are out! The day is about to get underway. The overnight batters Theunis de Bruyn and Temba Bavuma are ready. Dilruwan Perera has the ball in hand to start the proceedings. Let's play!

Pitch Report - Shaun Pollock out there says nothing's changed with regards to the surface. Adds that South Africa used a lot of the sweep shot on Day 3. Kepler Wessels with him mentions the importance of deploying the sweep shot, particularly the power sweep, provided you pick the right deliveries. States that for the leg side field, the reverse sweep, if employed correctly, could be a good option to disrupt the field. And ends saying if you can't sweep, just believe in your shots and rotate the strike.

Hello and welcome to the fourth day of the second and final Test match between Sri Lanka and South Africa at Sinhalese Sports Club, Colombo. This is probably the last day considering that the visitors have lost 5 crucial wickets on Day 3 and still are way behind the target. Only Theunis de Bruyn has shown some grit to hang around in the middle but other than him, everybody was in too much of a hurry to rest after a tiring day. Dean Elgar was given three lives, generously, but he failed to kick on and his 4th life faltered him. For the home team, Dilruwan Perera enjoyed his 'unlucky' birthday and managed to get into the wickets column along with his counterparts. It's highly unlikely that the target will be chased down or the Protea batters will bat for two days, but miracles happen when you least expect them to. At least that's what the team from Africa must feel. The first session starts in a while, hang around!
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Day 4 seems like it will be the final day of this Test, unless of course, de Bruyn and his remaining mates decide otherwise. To say it will be challenging, is putting it lightly. Though, in all honesty, it seems more a question of when it'll be wrapped up than how will South Africa manage through this storm. Still, it remains to be seen. Join us at 1000 local (0430 GMT) for all the exciting action. Till then, you can switch tabs and catch another Pakistan domination against Zimbabwe in the final ODI by switching tabs. Cheers!

The story was how everyone foresaw it. The spin trio ran through most of the Protea batting order, with all of them sharing the spoils. Theunis de Bruyn has been the only one who's looked assured, composed and equipped enough to deal with the Lankan spin attack. Rest all, capitulated when put under the pump. One would have expected, or rather, wanted more fight and grit from the Protea side which is deemed as a quality one. Not to be though.

A thoroughly satisfying day, particularly the final session, for Sri Lanka, as they walk off the field. The last couple of hours yielded 97 runs in 29 overs with 4 wickets falling. It was a rather eventful day to say the least, with everything happening. The South African openers were given lives, Elgar 3 of them, but they still couldn't make the most of it. What was to follow is not something any South African fan would have wanted to witness.
Drifting in on middle and then turning, de Bruyn is nicely place behind the line as he blocks it out. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Short and flat outside off, de Bruyn chops this square. Dilruwan at point moves swiftly to his left and dives to keep the ball from going past him. Lovely effort.
Swept away into the gap on the leg side for a single.
Lesser spin this time from Herath, Bavuma manages to keep it out without any trouble.
Behind a driving length, around off, turns away and beats the outside edge of Bavuma's hanging bat.
FOUR! Full ball attacking the stumps, Bavuma brings the broom out and sweeps it through square leg. A couple of runs result.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short ball outside off, cut away to the backward point fielder for nothing.
Slower through the air in line of the stumps, de Bruyn prods forward and defends it.
Gets behind the ball and blocks it.
Sweeps this from outside off towards square leg for a single.
Sharp turn from Perera. Lands this outside off and comes back in. Bavuma gets hit on his pad outside off.
The physios are out giving some treatment to the arm of de Bryun. And, Dilruwan Perera is called back to bowl.
Stays right behind the line and blocks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Similar ball, similar result.
Tossed up and it spins sharply outside off, de Bruyn is beaten.
Full and on the stumps, swept away on the leg side for one.
Loopy and full on off, blocked.
FOUR! The leg break but de Bruyn picks it up quickly. He rocks back, has room to free his arms outside off and slaps it through covers for a boundary.
On the back foot this time, works it down gently in front of short leg.
Full, straight, with a lot of air. Theunis shifts his weight onto his front foot and defends.
Temba stands tall and punches it firmly through the covers. The sweeper cuts it off by moving to his left and saves a run for his side.
Goes on the back foot and nudges it away into the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Well played, Big T. That's a very good shot. Goes with the spin, sweeps it through square leg. De Bruyn finds the fence without any problem.
Another sweep, a top edge this time but it's fallen safe. Over the man at backward square leg, brace taken.
Drives this full delivery to mid off.
FOUR! A lot of air on middle and leg, swept hard by Bavuma over backward square leg for a boundary.
Spinning away from around off, Temba is well inside the crease and has enough time to tap it down on the off side.
Short, flat and quick on off, de Bruyn goes back and whips this through the empty mid-wicket region. Single taken.
Full and loopy outside off, blocked nicely off the front foot.
Floated and turning in, Bavuma is caught low on the pads while trying to play at that.
Plays it with the spin and turns it away just wide of short leg.

An audacious shot from Bavuma. Completely unnecessary with the ball spinning so much. He premeditated the reverse way early, but the ball landed way too short for him to connect and it spun a long way down too. Luckily, his back leg didn't drag out because Dickwella took the bails off quickly.
Quicker through the air on off, Bavuma is well forward as he keeps this one out safely.
Temba Bavuma to bat next for South Africa. Two slips, a leg slip, a silly point and short leg in place for him.

OUT! Plumb! Maharaj departs for a golden duck. Off break just outside off, spins in and strikes Maharaj clean on the front pad as he tries to defend off the front foot. Loud shout, the finger goes up but Keshav reviews after a long chat with his partner. Maybe he thought there's an inside edge otherwise he'd never have gone for it. In any case, the replays roll in and they show he's gone. No edge of any kind involved and he is right in front of the sticks. Sri Lanka on the charge.
Review. For an lbw decision with Keshav Maharaj in question. He was given out and he took it upstairs. Let's see now...
Keshav Maharaj walks out.

OUT! This is a body blow to South Africa! Their captain, their best player on this tour, has departed. Landed on off, it goes on straight. Maybe the slightest of turns. Faf du Plessis takes a step across, presents a straight bat in defense and the ball goes behind to first slip off his pads. Now, an appeal goes up, mostly likely for a catch as the Lankans feel there is some bat involved. The umpire doesn't budge so the review is taken. Snicko detects the ball took the inside edge and that's that. Sri Lanka rejoice.
Short and wide, cut hard on the off side.
Premeditates the paddle sweep and ends up adjusting late due to the line. Well outside off, it's blocked.
Quite slow through the air, allows Theunis enough time to block it out.
Some room offered outside off on a fuller length, driven just wide of mid off for a run.
Sharp turn for Rangi! Dropped on off and it turns away with some venomous bounce. Du Plessis does well to drops his wrists and avoid it.
Landed on off, spinning, Faf plays inside the line and gets beaten.
On the leg stump line, worked down in front of short leg.
Full on the stumps again, played back down the track once more.
A lot of air on this, from around the wicket, forces de Bruyn foward as he mistimes the drive back to the bowler.
Whips this off the back foot well into the leg side for a single.
Floated on off, blocked out safely.
Off break on off, spins in sharply with some heavy bounce. Faf goes back and is caught high on the thigh pad.
Blocked out by the batsman to end the over.
Opens the face and pushes it to point.
Swept away behind square on the leg side for a double.
FOUR BYES! Leg break around off, kicks off the surface a bit and takes de Bruyn by surprise. He withdraws at the last moment and it goes right between the keeper and first slip for a boundary.
Meets the straighter one with a defensive bat in response.
There was an inside edge on that. Not sure why there aren't more men circling the batsman. Spinning in on the pads, goes off Faf's inside edge, then his pads and through leg gully. Single collected.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
De Bruyn picks up the straighter one, adjusts well at the last second and defends off the front foot.
Stays back and guards it out safely.
Moves a little across, gets low to this full ball and sweeps it down to short fine leg.
Goes deep inside the crease and works it just wide of FSL.
Straighter one from the bowler, worked down on the leg side.
Akila Dananjaya to have a change of ends.
Uses his feet to dance down and blocks it in front of covers.
Positions himself perfectly behind the line and blocks.
Full and straight from Rangi, Faf meets it with the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Shot. Too full on the stumps, du Plessis sweeps it through mid-wicket and finds the fence with ease.
Full around off, driven straight to the man at covers.
Skipper Faf du Plessis marches on in the eye of the storm. Going to take all from him to hang in there. His side needs him to.

OUT! A ripper! Rangana Herath makes his presence felt right away. Lands it on middle, it turns away from Amla's blade, beats the outside edge and uproots the off stump. Wrong choice from the South African veteran. Should have come forward when he went back. His off pole is lying on the ground and that's another wicket down.
Rangana Herath back on to bowl.
Meets the quicker ball with a defensive blade. Nice high elbow to block.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tightly kept out. De Bruyn prods forward and blocks it under his nose.
Full ball outside the line of off stump, pushed gently in front of covers.
Spins in a long way and goes off Theunis' pads past leg gully.
Quicker off break around off, de Bruyn moves across to get behind the line and defends it down.
Drilled just wide of mid off for a brisk run.
Tapped away square on the off side. No run taken.
Uses the depth of his crease to make room and works it away on the leg side for a single.
FOUR BYES! Spins down leg a long way, Amla leaves and it goes through everyone. It goes to the fence behind for a boundary.
Jumps out on the track, gets close to the pitch and pushes it to the left of the bowler.
Off spinner on middle, turns down the leg side, left alone by the batsman.
Drinks are on the field. Everybody could use a breather. Phew!
Floated and attacking the stumps, de Bruyn presses forward and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Hangs back deep inside the crease and defends.
Slower through the air on middle and leg, blocked down on the leg side.
Skips down the track like a ballerina and whips it away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Darted full, strikes Hashim low on the pads.
Flatter around off, punched off the back foot to covers for a run.
Turning in once more, goes off the pad and lobs into the hands of the man at leg gully. Appeal is not even bothered with. Another eventful over comes to an end.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
No ball! Another time when a spinner has overstepped. Uncanny. It's spinning down leg as Amla misses his tickle.
Off break again on the stumps, defended down on the leg side.

Not out! That was close. Really close. Impact has saved him. Dananjaya serves it around off and it turns in, raps Hashim Amla on the front pad as he misses his attempted sweep shot. Big shout, nothing from the umpire so the fielding side decides to take it upstairs. Replays roll in and they show that the impact is umpire's call, so Amla survives.
Review time. It's a close one, looks gone too to the naked eye. Hashim Amla is the man in the spotlight and it's up to the TV umpire to see if he's gone leg before or not.
FOUR! Excellent way of combating the off spinner. Amla makes good use of the feet to get close to the pitch and then sweetly drives it through extra cover for a boundary.
Off break outside off, catches Amla on the front pad well outside the line as he goes down to sweep. No use of the appeal in the end.
Just behind a driving length, on off, de Bruyn comes forward, not quite close to the pitch, hence mistimes the cover drive back down the track.
Drills this full delivery through the vacant spaces in the cover region. Comes back for the second quite comfortably.
Works it with the spin behind towards leg gully.
Switches to over the wicket, fires full on the stumps, Theunis barely manages to dig it out.
On the pads again as Dilruwan continues from around the wicket, worked straight to short leg.
Fuller and faster on the pads, worked to backward square leg. Dot ball.
Prods forward and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Darted extremely full on middle, de Bruyn goes deep in the crease and whips it back down the track. It hits his partner at the other end and rolls to mid off. Single taken.
The leg break this time, takes Theunis a little by surprise. Goes off the inside edge as he tries to play at it behind on the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Spinning in, it hits the batsman on the pads.
FOUR! Gives the charge, takes the aerial route and gets the desired result. Lofts it well over mid-wicket for a boundary. Nicely done by de Bruyn.
Amls moves across to defend it off the back foot.
This one is down the leg side and Amls leaves it alone.
Amla defends it from within the crease.
Hashim Amla is the next batsman in.

OUT! Can I just say that karma is a real thing? I am tempted to say so just because Dilruwan Perera, who literally give Elgar three chances, has finally managed to get him out. And today it's his birthday as well. Lucky charm perhaps! He bowls a flatter ball on off and pushes it up to the batsman. Elgar should have been on the front foot but for some reason, he went back. The ball skids through and hits him on his back leg. The umpire has no issue in raising his finger but for the record, he checks the no ball. Replays shows that he is fine now. Sri Lankans celebrate as if they have won the match. Elgar walks back with a saddening smile on his face.
Slower and bowled cleverly. Elgar has no answer to this. It lands on off and spin away from the left-hander. He hangs his bat it defense but is beaten ends up.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

In the air... but safe! De Bruyn and his tryst with sweep shot continues. He goes for it once again but the ball reaches him late. It gets the glove on its way towards leg slip. It lands safely once again luckily for him.
Lunges forward and keeps this one out.
Faster on middle, defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Five Runs! A gentle push to the point region by Elgar and they set off for a quick run. The fielder there has a shy at the stumps but it was poor throw at the keeper's end. The ball deflects off the de Bruyn's bat and beats Perera who is backing up there. The ball rolls to the boundary. Handy runs for South Africa.
Elgar has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
De Bruyn looks to sweep once again but fails to do so. The ball lobs in the air off his pad towards left of the leg slip. Some oohs and aahs from the Lankan again.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.
Goes straight. Phew! De Bruyn has no idea where it'll spin and he just plays the line but it goes whizzes past the outside edge into the gloves of keeper.
Full, driven through mid on for another single.
Does well here. First he comes down the track to play the big shot perhaps but seeing the shot length, he tucked it gently in the corner on the on side and changes strike.
De Bruyn uses his wrist to work this one to the on side.
A tad shorter around on off, cut to point for no run.
In the line of this delivery and blocks it.
Pushes the full ball through mid off for a run.
Elgar flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
It hit a crack or something here. Pitched around off, it lands and grips or hits the crack and turns sharply from the left-hander who was looking to play the line. Another miss for him.
Hangs back and bunts it out.
Defends the ball in front of his eyes.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Gets the conventional sweep out and connects it well this time. He should feel better after this one as the ball races to the square leg fence.
Beaten all ends up! That's a jaffa from Perera. It pitches around off and straightens from there. Elgar plays for the line as he should but is beaten. He survives again!
On the pads, tucked to square leg for a single.
Shortish, pushed to covers for a single.
Full and on the pads, swept through square leg. Silva out in the deep moves to his right and dives to keep the ball inside the rope. Two runs taken.
Landed short and turning in from around off, de Bruyn is on the back foot as he rocks back and works it down just in front of short leg.
Plays with the spin and turns it away on the leg side.
Works it off the pads and gets to the other end for a single.
Ripper! Play that, Dean Elgar! Kicked right off the deck and turns heavily. The southpaw can only evade it barely.
Shouts for a leg before but it's turned down, rightly so too. Sliding in on leg, it keeps going down with the angle, Elgar is caught on the pads and a loud appeal goes up.
First change for Sri Lanka. Akila Dananjaya is on with two slips and a short leg.

Was this another chance? According to the Lankans it was. De Bruyn comes forward again to defend but fails to reach the ball. As a result, it spins in, takes bat-pad and lobs to the left of the diving FSL fielder.
Half forward is de Bruyn, he works the ball uppishly to the on side.
Extra bounce and spin into the right-hander. It hit him on his thigh pad.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Comes forward and defends.
A tad shorter delivery in line of the stumps, defended off the back foot.
Elgar is half forward to play this one and ends up getting an inside edge on to his pads.
Not out says the umpire. A fullish ball around off, he looks to defend but misses it. The ball hits him on his pads and the Lankans erupt in appeal but the impact is outside off.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Out comes the sweep once again from de Bruyn. It has been a handy weapon for him. He sweeps the full ball though mid-wicket and earns a boundary.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Rocks back and works it off his back foot.
Around off, played to the point region. What an over this has been.
He fails to connect to the one outside his off stump.

No ball! What drama! Are you kidding me? This is unbelievable. How could you, Perera? How could you? Ooh! So let me try to explain what happened. Elgar moved back to play the cut to the shortish ball but ended up nicking it to Dickwella behind the stumps. The Sri Lankans rejoiced and Hashim Amla was on his way. He walked out in the middle as well but hang on... the third umpire checked for the front foot no ball and guess what! It's again on the line and the line belongs to the umpire. It's a no ball! Second one from Dilruwan, against the same batsman. As soon as the umpire had the confirmation, he called Elgar back. Amla walked back and gave Dean a fist bump on his way.
Flatter on off, defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around off, another miss from Elgar. He shouldn't worry too much about these misses and carry on the work for the sake of South Africa.
Lunges forward and keeps it out.
De Bruyn has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Sweeps this one but doesn't get it away this time. It lobs to adjacent to the pitch.
Played to the point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

FOUR! Cheeky from Elgar. He connected to the fuller ball nicely and reverse swept it through cover-point. A boundary to Elgar. This will frustrate Herath a bit but perhaps not too much considering how many runs he has to play with.
Around off, easily defended down the track.
An attempted reserve sweep but gets hit on the arm. Herath vs Elgar and he has a way to tackle him perhaps.
Gets behind the line and blocks it out.
FOUR! Reverse ramp shot this from de Bruyn. He has done well to guide this one fine through the third man region. It was too full form Perera and the batsman made the most of it. A boundary.
Drives the full ball through cover-point. A run results.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Flighted in line of the stumps, pushed to covers. Two runs taken.
Fullish on off, defended.
Dilruwan Perera to continue from the other end.

Fuller in line of the stumps, de Bruyn gets an inside edge and it falls wide of FSL. End of the first over after the Tea break. The over rate should be excellent considering the spinners will be bowling from both ends.
On the pads, flicked through mid-wicket by Elgar. One run taken.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Around off, easily defended by Elgar.
Gets behind the line and bunts it out off the front foot.
On off, blocked to the on side.
We're back for the last session of the day. Theunis de Bruyn and Dean Elgar are out in the middle. Rangana Herath will continue with the ball.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

An eventful session to say the least. After setting a massive target of 490 in front of the Proteas, the Lankans came out with intent. The spin arsenal dismissed Markram, but they easily could have had one or two more. Elgar survived a scare, and de Bruyn is barely hanging in right now too. It's going to be a damning challenge for the visiting team, one of the toughest they have faced. It's going to take all they have to survive the trail by spin. Join us in a very short while for the final session of Day 3.

This one goes the other way. De Bruyn is bamboozled. He comes on to the front foot to play the defensive shot but it hits him on his pads. The ball lobs to leg gully who takes a diving catch. Nothing doing says the umpire. THAT'S TEA ON DAY 3.

And he survives again! What is going on, de Bruyn? He has no idea where the ball is going to turn. Perera bowls a similar delivery to the last one and de Bruyn misses it in a similar fashion. Only change was that he got hit a touch lower on his back leg as he was crouching down. This time the bowler looks confident though and Lakmal takes the review once again. The replays roll in. It stats the same story as the previous ball. It lands on leg stump, goes towards off, hits him in line and juts clips the outer half of the off pole. The on-field umpire's decision stays. Theunis has luck on his side today.
Another review from Sri Lanka. Same man in question for the LBW decision.

FOUR LEG BYES! He survives. But what a beauty this has been from Perera. He bowls this from 'round the wicket, and straightens this one from the leg stump. De Bruyn plays for the line but misses it to get hit on his back pad. An appeal ensues from Dickwella but the bowler doesn't look too interested. He forces Lakmal for the review who goes for it. The replays comes in. The ball lands on leg stump, goes with the angle, hits him in line but just clips the outside half of the off stump. The original decision from the umpire was not out and the decision won't be turned around. Sri Lanka though retain the review.
A review has been taken. Theunis de Bruyn is the man in question for the LBW.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Gets behind the line of this one and keeps it out.
Driven through mid off by Elgar.
Goodness me! Vicious spin from Herath. He drags his length back a touch, the ball lands and spins further away from the off stump. Good over for South Africa though.
FOUR! Second boundary of the over. De Bruyn has swept Herath clean through mid-wicket. He isn't going to just block, block and block.
Too full, eased to mid on for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Just as the fielder from point was moved finer, Elgar executed the reverse sweep to perfection. Herath bowled this one outside off on a length, it spins further into the stumps but Elgar has other ideas to play it. If the conventional sweep doesn't work, than reverse sweep should. And it has.
Fails to connect his reverse sweep with the fullish ball.
Too straight on the pads, flicked to the fine leg region for a run. Elgar keeps strike.
Elgar was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Comes forward to the flighted ball and defends it.
A touch short this, tucked to the on side by Dean.
Gets forward and bunts it to the on side for no run.
Elgar goes on the back foot and taps it to off side.
Gets behind the line of this one and blocks it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! He picked this one up nicely. A flighted ball in line of the stumps, de Bruyn sweeps it hard and gets it through the mid-wicket region. A boundary to him.
Comes in with the angle, de Bruyn gets an inside edge onto his pad. No harm done.
De Bruyn lets the ball go outside his off stump.

OUT! Herath has his man this time. Markram though should be criticized for this loose shot. He played across the full ball to get hit on the pads as he missed it altogether. He looked at his partner who perhaps told him that he can't be more plumb than this. So, finally, Sri Lanka have the first wicket after handing out a couple of chances.
In comes Theunis de Bruyn at no.3.
Flatter on off, defended.
No Ball! No ball shouts the umpire. A length ball around off, cut to covers for no run.
On the pads, tucked to mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Good use of the feet from Markram here. He gets to the pitch of the ball and hits it straight past the bowler. A boundary results through the long off region.
Around off, Markram lunges forward to block it.
Shortish around off, guided to the third man region for a run.
Flatter on middle, defended.
FOUR! A bit too full from Rangana Herath, Markram whips it hard through mid-wicket and finds the fence. Eventful over comes to an end.
Full and just outside off, blocked.
Flights this well up outside off, draws Markram forward and beats the outside edge. Mathews collects it this time, but to his dismay there was no edge.
Tossed up delivery well outside off, left alone.
Quicker and shorter on off, Aiden goes deep inside the crease and guards it out.

Dropped! That's a sitter. Mathews of all people should have taken that. Now both the South African openers have got a life. Herath beautifully tosses it up around off and it turns away ever so slightly. Markram is forward and gets an edge behind. Should have been a regulation catch for Angelo, but he drops it.
Flicks this through leg slip for no run.
Keeps it out off the inner edge this time.

BOWLED BUT IT'S A NO BALL! Elgar's safe! He will be feeling lucky. Big time. From around the wicket, Dilruwan drifts it in from around off, this one doesn't turn away and keeps coming in with the angle. Elgar kneels down and brings out the big slog sweep, to everyone's surprise, and he pays the price for that as the stumps are rattled behind. The umpire just checks upstairs for the front foot no ball and... much to Dean's delight, the offie has overstepped. Big sigh of relief for the southpaw. He'll want to make it count now.
Nicely done. Gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Quicker and attacking the stumps, blocked with a straight blade.
Nicely drifting in at first around off before turning away, Elgar covers the line and leaves.
Full and darted on the pads, worked behind square leg for nothing.
Defended off the front foot by Aiden presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller, driven to covers for no run.
Goes past the blade again. It pitches, grips and spins away from the right-hander.
Hangs back and bunts it out.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Just short! Markram comes down the track to push it. He gets it to covers but a fielder there dives forward. He still couldn't reach it. Markram escapes!
Wowza! This one spun, bounced and beat the outside edge. Vicious from Perera. He kept this just outside off, Elgar came forward but failed to connect with the ball.
Rocks back and bunts it out to the on side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
So close to the off pole but it will be considered a very good leave from Elgar.
Shortish around off, cut to point.
Gets behind the line and defends it.

FOUR! Edged but in the gap! How many chances in this over? At least three. This one was bowled fuller around off, slower through the air and got the edge of Markram's bat. But kudos to the batsman who played it with soft hands which saved him eventually. The ball went through the slip cordon and rushed to the boundary.
Outside off, left alone.
Markram has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

In the air... and dropped! Perera the culprit. Herath made Elgar play the sweep once again. The ball, however, went high in the air towards square leg. Dilruwan ran from fine leg towards square leg, reached there in time, put both his hands to it but failed to collect it. One run taken.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.

So close! Had Lakmal hit the stumps at the bowler's end, Markram would've been a goner. A fullish ball around off, Markram pushes it to mid on and sets off for a run. Lakmal there was quick to react, picks it up and has a shy. Luckily, Markram survives to fight another day.
FOUR! Plonked by Elgar. A touch too full from Perera and Elgar slogs it across the line and gets it through mid-wicket. First boundary of the South African innings.
Flatter outside, goes past the blade.
Dangerous this from Elgar. He looks to play the sweep against the spin. He gets it off his arm behind the keeper. In the end, no harm done.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.
Similar ball on middle, defended.
Floated on leg, Elgar gets back behind the line and blocks it.
Dilruwan Perera to bowl from the other end.

Beaten! This is scintillating bowling from the veteran. Tossed up outside off, spins away just a touch and beats the outside edge of Markram's bat. Dickwella collects the ball and knocks the stumps from its roots.
Presses forward and smothers the ball in its tracks.
Goes full again, nice and loopy around off, Markram is rock solid in defense.
Drags his length back a touch, Markram is forced to go back and block it out.
Tossed up with some nice shape on it, Elgar steps out of the crease and works it away to mid-wicket for a single. Off the mark with that.
Looped up nicely by Herath, Elgar is well forward in defense.
